title: How an overlooked geothermal plant got a second chance
gist: Zanskar revived a failing 15-MW New Mexico geothermal plant by using advanced subsurface modeling to drill a deeper, better-placed 8,000-foot well, doubling output and overturning the industry assumption that deeper drilling sacrifices water flow. The implication is that overlooked conventional hydrothermal assets across the US may be worth far more than enhanced-geothermal hype suggests.

insights.claim: A small company called Zanskar bought a rapidly failing geothermal power plant in New Mexico in June 2024 and, two years later, has it running at full capacity again on the strength of a single new well.
insights.so_what: Distressed operating geothermal assets can be bought cheap and re-rated with subsurface engineering — an acquisition play, not a greenfield one.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart

insights.claim: Lightning Dock's reservoir was cooling at roughly 10 °F per year — a 50 °F drop over five years — against an industry-typical decline rate of 1 to 2 °F per year.
insights.so_what: Anomalous decline rates flag mis-drilled rather than depleted reservoirs, which is exactly the screen for cheap turnaround acquisitions.
insights.quote: Lightning Dock saw temperatures drop by 50 °F over five years, a rate of 10 °F per year
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart

insights.claim: At acquisition the water entering the plant was just 250 °F while the plant had been designed to run on at least 310 °F, leaving the facility uneconomical to operate.
insights.so_what: The 60 °F gap quantifies how thin the margin is between a stranded geothermal asset and a working one.
insights.locator: When the company purchased the facility
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart

insights.claim: Over the past year of operation the revived plant generated more than twice the electricity it would have produced with the old wells, from a 15-megawatt facility feeding the local grid.
insights.so_what: A 2x output uplift from one well is the kind of unit economics that justifies a roll-up of underperforming hydrothermal plants.
insights.quote: Lightning Dock generated over twice the electricity it would have with the old wells
insights.locator: Over the past year of operation
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart

insights.claim: The new well reaches 8,000 feet, began operating in May 2025, and after a full year is still flowing at more than 4,000 gallons per minute.
insights.so_what: Sustained flow after a full year is the durability evidence lenders and offtakers need before financing similar retrofits.
insights.quote: After a full year, the well is still flowing at more than 4,000 gallons per minute.
insights.locator: The team drilled a new well
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart

themes.theme: Subsurface diagnosis as the real bottleneck

insights.claim: Advanced modeling revealed that the site's two original production wells were only 2,500 feet deep, poorly located, and hitting nothing but the very top of the underground reservoir.
insights.so_what: The binding constraint was well placement, not resource quality — meaning the value creation lever is software and subsurface interpretation, not new geology.
insights.quote: the wells were only hitting the very top of the reservoir there
insights.locator: When Zanskar mapped the underground conditions
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart

insights.claim: Conventional geothermal economics hinge on a narrow physical window: water must flow through fractured hot rock in sufficient volume and at sufficient temperature, or the power plant simply cannot run efficiently.
insights.so_what: Two variables — temperature and flow — determine whether a geothermal asset is worth anything, and both are addressable by drilling decisions.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart

insights.claim: Confidence in geothermal asset performance requires multi-year operating records, so early results should be treated as provisional even when they look strong.
insights.so_what: Underwriting geothermal turnarounds on one year of flow data carries real duration risk; watch for decline-curve updates.
insights.quote: Ultimately you need to run these things for long time frames to get confidence in their performance over long time frames
insights.locator: The data so far shows that the plant
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart

insights.claim: The conventional wisdom that drilling deeper buys heat at the cost of flow — because deeper rock is packed tighter — failed at this site, where flow actually increased at the deeper new well.
insights.so_what: If the depth-flow tradeoff is weaker than assumed, the recoverable resource base under existing US hydrothermal plants is materially larger than currently modeled.
insights.quote: What the team found, however, was that the flow actually increased in the area where they drilled the new well.
insights.locator: The conventional wisdom in geothermal energy
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart

insights.claim: A single well result is being framed as changing how the entire class of American hydrothermal assets should be valued, not just this one plant.
insights.so_what: Watch for repeat wells at other legacy sites; confirmation would reprice a whole category of overlooked infrastructure.
insights.quote: That fundamentally changes how you think about not just Lightning Dock but all hydrothermal assets in America and what the potential can be for all of them
insights.locator: That fundamentally changes how you think
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart

themes.theme: Oil-and-gas learning curve migrating into geothermal

insights.claim: Oil and gas moved from near-surface production to wells stretching 20,000 feet or more over recent decades, and the same depth arc is expected to play out in geothermal.
insights.so_what: Directional signal for drilling-services demand: geothermal well depth, and therefore spend per well, has structural room to rise.
insights.quote: I think that arc is going to play out in geothermal
insights.locator: Oil and gas developers have chased resources
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart

insights.claim: Typical geothermal well fields today run 3,000 to 5,000 feet deep, so the 8,000-foot well at Lightning Dock sits well outside current industry practice.
insights.so_what: Quantifies the gap between standard practice and what modern drilling makes possible — the arbitrage window for early movers.
insights.locator: While typical geothermal well fields range
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart

themes.theme: Conventional revival versus enhanced geothermal hype

insights.claim: While buzz and investment have concentrated on enhanced geothermal systems such as Fervo Energy's fracking-based approach, plenty of low-hanging fruit remains in conventional hydrothermal resources that simply need a second look.
insights.so_what: Capital is crowding into the technically hardest part of geothermal while cheaper brownfield returns sit unclaimed — a valuation dislocation worth screening for.
insights.quote: there’s still plenty of “low-hanging fruit” in the geothermal world
insights.locator: There’s been a lot of buzz and investment
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart

insights.claim: Further upside at the same site is planned: a few more years of development plus a power plant upgrade could raise output beyond the current doubling.
insights.so_what: Surface-equipment upgrades are a second, cheaper layer of value creation stacked on top of the drilling fix.
insights.locator: The company plans to do further development
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart

insights.claim: Geothermal's strategic pull is that it supplies emissions-free electricity available 24-7, positioning it against intermittent renewables rather than alongside them.
insights.so_what: Firm clean baseload is the scarce product in power markets; geothermal competes for the same premium as nuclear and storage.
insights.locator: As the world looks for more sources
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
